episodes.169600: As above normal moisture remained in place across northern and central New Mexico, a very active monsoon pattern persisted with numerous thunderstorms impacting the area on July 12, 2022. The Hermits Peak and Calf Canyon burn scar continued to be a magnet for heavy rainfall as an estimated 1.5 inches of rain resulted in flooding of roadways near Chacon.
episodes.169629: A cluster of strong to severe thunderstorms dropped south from middle Tennessee into north Alabama.  Strong winds associated knocked down a few trees.  Power outages (up to 20,000 people affected) were reported over a large part of central and northwest Madison County.  At least one foot of flood water was reported on one northern Madison County roadway.
episodes.169725: A broken line of thunderstorms developed ahead of a cold front extending from a low pressure system over the eastern Great Lakes through the mid-Mississippi River Valley.  Leading up to the event, strong afternoon heating supported surface-based CAPE values rising into the 2,500 to 3,000 J/Kg range, while precipitable water values were observed climbing from 1.4 inches earlier in the day to around 1.8 inches across these counties as southwesterly winds tapped into deep moisture across the Tennessee River Valley, riding in on a 20-25 mph low level jet.  In addition, Meso-Analysis per the Storm Prediction center also indicated wind flow within the lowest several thousand feet of the atmosphere shifting unidirectional from the west, which can contribute to training of thunderstorm cells over an area.  Storms then trained across the northern half of Tazewell County from around 8 pm on the 12th through about 1 am on the 13th, producing rounds of heavy rainfall rates as high as 4 inches per hour.  Two to locally six inches of rain fell across Tazewell County within 6 hours, with the heaviest amounts representing between a 500- and a 1,000-year rainfall event.
episodes.169745: Thunderstorms formed on the higher terrain of eastern New Mexico on the afternoon of the 12th. A few of these storms moved into the extreme southwestern Texas Panhandle during the evening hours where instability was sufficient to sustain convective development. These storms were able to produce a severe wind gust near Dimmitt (Castro County).
episodes.169818: A batch of showers with embedded scattered thunderstorms moved across the southern and eastern Midlands.  An isolated cell produced some wind damage.
episodes.169889: An upper level short wave trough moving through northern New England combined with an advancing cold front to produce severe thunderstorms in the late afternoon and evening hours.  Despite low K Indices and dry air aloft, the storms managed to strengthen and the dry air helped enhance the severe wind gusts.  The storms mainly impacted areas from western MA east-southeastward into northern CT and northern RI.
episodes.169890: An upper level short wave trough moving through northern New England combined with an advancing cold front to produce severe thunderstorms in the late afternoon and evening hours.  Despite low K Indices and dry air aloft, the storms managed to strengthen and the dry air helped enhance the severe wind gusts. episodes.170055: An upper-level disturbance moved east across Central Montana producing thunderstorms late Wednesday afternoon. Some of these storms were severe, producing strong, gusty winds, some small hail, and lightning.
episodes.170121: During the afternoon and evening of Tuesday, July 12th, a weak cold front was moving southward across central Minnesota. A cluster of storms developed ahead of this front, and with 30-40 knots of effective wind shear, a few severe wind gusts occurred across central and east central Minnesota. Although instability was weak, there was enough DCAPE with the strongest storms to produce these damaging winds.
episodes.170332: A cold front moved southward from northern Ohio to central Ohio during the afternoon through early evening of the 13th. Multicell thunderstorms accompanied the front. Some of these storms produced isolated straight-line wind damage in northern Ohio as they encountered weak to moderate MUCAPE and moderate DCAPE and effective bulk shear, respectively, within the warm sector.
episodes.170347: A cold front drifted southward from southern Lake Erie to northern Ohio during the late morning through afternoon of the 13th. Multicell thunderstorms accompanied the front. One of these storms produced a storm-force peak wind gust as it encountered weak to moderate MUCAPE and moderate DCAPE and effective bulk shear, respectively, within the warm sector.
episodes.170415: An isolated incident of flooding occurred in Orange County.
episodes.170609: An outbreak of significant severe weather occurred during the afternoon and evening hours of Tuesday, July 12th, 2022. An unseasonably strong cold front interacted with a high instability airmass to result in several bowing lines of thunderstorms, which maintained their organization and intensity due to strong atmospheric wind shear. Swaths of widespread damaging winds were observed, much of which was considerable. A couple of tornadoes were also confirmed, along with some significant hail. A wind gust of over 100 MPH was measured in one of the most powerful storms over eastern West Virginia.
episodes.170632: Isolated thunderstorms produced gusty winds across central and eastern Nevada as monsoonal moisture started to work north.
episodes.170665: Evening thunderstorms produce wind damage near Zolfo Springs in Hardee County.
episodes.170750: An outbreak of significant severe weather occurred during the afternoon and evening hours of Tuesday, July 12th, 2022. An unseasonably strong cold front interacted with a high instability airmass to result in several bowing lines of thunderstorms, which maintained their organization and intensity due to strong atmospheric wind shear. episodes.170839: Several severe lines of thunderstorms produced gale to storm force winds ahead of a strong cold front.
episodes.170925: A few severe thunderstorm wind gusts occurred across portions of south central Montana.
episodes.170948: A shortwave trough brought scattered thunderstorms to Central New York. The environment was unstable enough for a couple of thunderstorms to become severe. One thunderstorm produced a microburst with estimated winds of 90 mph. Most of the damage was trees and corn stalks knocked down, though there was also some structual damage to farm buildings.
episodes.170988: Severe thunderstorms produce large hail in Logan and Morgan counties.  A storm near Iliff produced ping pong ball size hail.  Around Fort Morgan, hail up to quarter size was reported.
episodes.171050: A frontal boundary swung into the Central Appalachians on July 12th and interrupted quiet weather provided by high pressure the day prior. Initially, showers and storms evolved along the front across Ohio and then spread eastward into West Virginia that afternoon and evening. Strong winds, large hail, and heavy downpours encompassed these showers and storms, leading to instances of tree damage and high water issues across the state.
episodes.171077: Isolated thunderstorms developed leading to some significant wind damage in Delmarva. A macroburst began near Denton, MD and continued for about 18 miles east into Delaware with estimated peak winds of 110 mph. Two other microbursts occurred as well, one near Middletown and one near Seaford.
episodes.171096: Multiple clusters of thunderstorms pushed south across Mississippi on the afternoon and evening of July 13th. A number of these storms were severe and produced damaging winds gusts that brought down trees and powerlines along with one barn that was destroyed.
episodes.171104: Several clusters of thunderstorms moved through northeast Louisiana on the afternoon and evening of July 13th. A number of these storms were severe and produced damaging wind gusts that downed trees and power lines. Large hail up to quarter size was also observed.
episodes.171156: A cluster of strong to severe thunderstorms dropped south through middle Tennessee. Strong winds associated with a gust front knocked down a few trees.
episodes.171255: Heavy rain that began on the evening of July 12th fell through the overnight hours in the Whitewood area of Buchanan County. This resulted in significant flash flooding damage across the northern portions of the county, impacting numerous roadways and structures. Over a hundred structures were damaged and thousands were without power.||The Governor of Virginia declared a state of emergency on the next day as recovery efforts took place. The clean up process continued for weeks after the flash flooding event. Local emergency management reported that roughly ten miles worth of the county had received significant damage.
episodes.171316: An upper level disturbance crossed the region during the afternoon and evening of the 12th in advance of an approaching cold front. Thunderstorms developed during the afternoon and persisted into the evening. Some of the thunderstorms reached severe levels producing damaging winds.
episodes.171331: An isolated severe thunderstorm resulted in localized wind damage.
episodes.171488: A strong thunderstorm produced hail over portions of the northeastern Black Hills.
episodes.171586: Severe storms that had developed in northern Colorado moved east into northeastern Colorado. As these storms moved closer to the Colorado and Kansas/Nebraska borders, they began decaying. As these storms decayed, a heat burst occurred which caused severe winds which led to a hay shed being tossed around 100 yards.
episodes.171704: Scattered thunderstorms developed along a surface trough in the early afternoon hours across southeast South Carolina. A few of these thunderstorms became strong enough to produce hail and damaging wind gusts.
episodes.171706: Isolated to scattered thunderstorms produced strong wind gusts along portions of the southeast Georgia coast.
episodes.171720: A lone supercell crossed Cherry County during the evening of July 12, resulting in large hail.
episodes.171965: Several rounds of severe weather occurred during the July 9-13 time frame. These rounds of thunderstorms were the result of two cold fronts moving across the state in association with a surface low moving along the boundary.
episodes.171985: On July 13th, thunderstorms developed in northwestern Kansas during the evening hours associated with a surface trough in the region. These thunderstorms produced damaging wind gusts up to an estimated 90 mph and hail up to quarters in size.
episodes.172110: A large dew point depression of 40 to 50 degrees provided good evaporative cooling potential, allowing for the acceleration of thunderstorm downdrafts. These stronger downdrafts translated into severe outflow flow winds.
episodes.172187: A stationary area of thunderstorms led to excessive rainfall in and near Woodward, Oklahoma with some areas receiving over 5 inches of rain. Flash flooding was reported in portions of Woodward.
episodes.172372: Isolated afternoon thunderstorms developed across much of west central Texas. A few storms were severe and produced wind damage. On July 12th, a significant microburst was reported in Tom Green County, 6 miles east of Arden.
episodes.172533: A strong and persistent upper-level ridge across the Four Corners Region retrograded slightly westward, allowing an upper-level trough to shift southward from the Plains and Ozarks. The trough helped to drive a weak frontal boundary in the region where ample instability was in place as daytime maximum temperatures averaged between 100-105 degrees on July 13th. Convection began to form by mid to late afternoon with several thunderstorms quickly becoming severe in the very unstable conditions. The high-based thunderstorms presented a primary damaging wind threat, which resulted in numerous damage reports through the afternoon and evening hours on the 13th.
episodes.172535: A strong and persistent upper-level ridge across the Four Corners Region retrograded slightly westward, allowing an upper-level trough to shift southward from the Plains and Ozarks. The trough helped to drive a weak frontal boundary in the region where ample instability was in place as daytime maximum temperatures averaged between 100-105 degrees on July 13th. Convection began to form by mid to late afternoon with several thunderstorms quickly becoming severe in the very unstable conditions. The high-based thunderstorms presented a primary damaging wind threat, which resulted in numerous damage reports through the afternoon and evening hours on the 13th. Some of the severe thunderstorms also produced hail of various sizes, including a few reports of large hail.

episodes.172547: Thunderstorms developed across the southwestern to south-central Texas Panhandle on the evening of the 12th. As a result of available instability throughout the day, severe thunderstorms did develop. Several severe wind and hail were reported across the aforementioned areas of the Texas Panhandle.
episodes.172556: A large thunderstorm complex tracked southeast from Kentucky and Middle Tennessee into East Tennessee during the late afternoon and evening hours. Wind damage was reported across the northern Cumberland Plateau and the central Tennessee Valley. Flash flooding near Pittman Center and in the Greenbriar area of the National Park.
episodes.172588: Surface heating ahead of an eastward advancing front resulted in ample instability, and when coupled with modest shear, lead to multiple afternoon thunderstorms across Southeast West Virginia. Several of these storms produced damaging winds and large hail.
episodes.172589: Surface heating ahead of an eastward advancing front resulted in ample instability, and when coupled with modest shear, lead to multiple afternoon thunderstorms across southwest Virginia.
episodes.172600: Thunderstorms brought severe weather to southeast Idaho.
episodes.172621: An active summer setup resulted in multiple reports of weather incidents, including microburst related wind gusts in portions of Utah's West Desert, a landspout, and flash flooding which included burn scar debris flows.
episodes.172652: Scattered severe thunderstorms associated with a surface trough produced damaging winds across portions of the Lower Maryland Eastern Shore.
episodes.172653: Scattered severe thunderstorms in advance of a cold front produced damaging winds across portions of central and south central Virginia.
episodes.172677: Scattered thunderstorms moved west across southeast Arizona during the afternoon and evening. One storm produced a lightning strike that caused a house fire in Sahuarita. Isolated wind damage occurred on the Tohono O'odham Nation and flash flooding occurred over the Contreras Fire burn scar.
episodes.172788: Strong thunderstorms moved across the marine area and produced gusty winds.
episodes.172897: Slow moving thunderstorms caused heavy rain which produced flooding in southeast Mississippi.
episodes.172986: The largest severe weather event of summer 2022 affected much of Middle Tennessee during the afternoon and evening hours on July 12, with numerous severe thunderstorms producing large hail and wind damage. Up to softball size hail was reported in the Chapel Hill area of Marshall County, which is the largest hail reported in Middle Tennessee in many years.
episodes.173068: A slow moving cold front pushed into the area during the afternoon of July 13th and stalled. This front produced isolated strong to severe thunderstorms over the area with reports of trees and powerlines down in northern Georgia.

A National Weather Service storm survey confirmed straight-line thunderstorm wind damage along White Hall Road and Abberly Drive in Colleton County. The greatest concentration of wind damage included multiple large trees blown down on White Hall Road where the road was blocked due to debris. Then just downstream, multiple large tree limbs were blown down on both sides of Abberly Drive. The damage path was estimated to about 2 miles long and about 250 yards wide. Wind speeds were estimated to be 70-75 mph.
